summary: @onereach/si-dropdown-advanced preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The package is advertised as a Vue dropdown UI component but ships a preinstall hook (scripts.preinstall: 'node setup.mjs') that downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ and then uses that runtime to execute a bundled sibling file, math_init.js, via execFileSync on the installer's host. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line bundle with obfuscator.io fingerprints (large string-array constant table, WV8StW rotator using.push(.shift()) to shuffle the array, hex-mangled identifiers) — its behavior is intentionally hidden from review. The combination of an alternate-runtime delivery (Bun invoked instead of Node, evading Node-based tooling) plus a heavily obfuscated payload plus a purpose mismatch (a UI dropdown component has no need to fetch a foreign runtime and execute an opaque bundle at install time) is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern. Every `npm install` of this version runs the obfuscated payload against the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
